title: Types of friction (ঘর্ষণের প্রকারভেদ)
placement: Book pages 89–90, topic 3.9.1: ঘর্ষণের প্রকারভেদ (Types of Friction): স্থিতি, গতি ও আবর্ত ঘর্ষণ. Next to the three definitions with fₛ = μₛN and fₖ = μₖN, and the rolling-friction paragraph (suitcase wheels).
description: The three kinds of friction in ONE scene (ঘর্ষণের প্রকারভেদ, pages 89–90, 3.9.1): the same 2 kg wooden block as in friction-force is pushed with a force gauge (বলমাপক). Tap by tap the push grows (3, 6, 9 N) and the block does not move: the crimson friction arrow under it grows to match the push exactly, the static friction (স্থিতি ঘর্ষণ). At 9.8 N the block gives way; the person eases off to keep a steady pace and the gauge falls to 7.8 N, the kinetic friction (গতি ঘর্ষণ), a faint arrow keeping the old 9.8 N for comparison. Then the block is lifted onto a small trolley with wheels and pushed again: it rolls on about 1 N, the rolling friction (আবর্ত ঘর্ষণ), the smallest of the three (suitcase wheels). The panel is one action, one result, one rule: a row of the book's three terms with the friction found under each (9.8, 7.8, 1 N), one numbered button whose same badge rings the block, a result line and a rule that grows in plain words (ঠেলা, ঘর্ষণ, পিছলে চলা, গড়িয়ে চলা) and ends with f_s = μ_s N and f_k = μ_k N, N explained as the surface's push up (equal to the weight) and μ as how rough the surface is. μ_s = 0.5, μ_k = 0.4 and 0.05 on wheels are example numbers (the book gives none; a note on the view says so). Test tab: 5 questions on scenes set up for them (the friction while the block is held by a push read off the gauge, the friction at a steady slide, which of the three frictions is acting, how much push a loaded block needs, why wheels make a suitcase easy to pull).
